en: General Preface to the *Dharmadhātu-krama-prathama-mukha* (The First Gate of the Sequence of the Dharma Realm).
At Tiantai Mountain’s Xiuchan Monastery, the śramaṇa Śākyamuni Zhiyi has, based upon the sūtras and supplemented by the treatises,
compiled the *Dharmadhātu-krama-prathama-mukha* in three hundred sections, arranged into seven fascicles, for circulation among those newly entering the study of the Way.
Briefly, there are three points.
First, for those who read the sutras and search the treatises and encounter various dharma-gates,
yet may become confused regarding their names and enumerations.
Second, it is for those who have not yet understood the sequence of the shallow and deep levels of the dharma-gates established by the holy teachings.
Third, it is for those who study the three contemplations (*trivipaśyanā*),
who should [rely] upon these various names, characteristics, and principles of the dharmas.
If one proceeds through each thought one by one, transforming them as they arise,
then contemplative understanding will be unimpeded and one will not be deluded when encountering sensory objects.
If, within a single thought-moment,
one penetrates all Buddha-dharmas,
then the three contemplations will naturally become clear and distinct.
Therefore, these three hundred treatises have been produced;
their names and teachings remain appropriate.
Below, I shall briefly distinguish their essential natures and characteristics.
I have now obtained three fascicles:
Chapter One, "The Initial Gate of Name-and-Form";
Chapter Two, "The Initial Gate of the Five Aggregates."
